title: Orata al cartoccio
subtitle: Bream baked in a paper parcel
excerpt: A whole sea bream sealed in a parchment parcel with olives, capers, cherry tomatoes, white wine, and herbs, then baked until the parcel puffs and the fish inside is perfectly steamed. Simple and spectacular.
sourceNotes: Al cartoccio (in a parcel) is a widespread Italian technique for cooking whole fish; orata (gilt-head bream) is the classic choice. Cross-referenced with Giorgio Locatelli, Made in Italy (2006) and Anna Del Conte, Gastronomy of Italy (1987).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The parcel can be assembled up to 2 hours ahead and refrigerated. Bake straight from the fridge, adding 5 extra minutes.

content.text: Orata al cartoccio is a forgiving and elegant way to cook a whole fish. The sealed parcel creates a steam environment that keeps the flesh moist and concentrates the flavours of the olive oil, wine, and aromatics. The parcel puffs dramatically in the oven and is opened at the table. Sea bream is the traditional choice; sea bass works equally well.

items.prepNote: 600 to 800 g, gutted and scaled; ask the fishmonger to prepare

content.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan (180°C conventional, gas 6). Score the fish 3 times on each side with a sharp knife.
Lay a large sheet of baking parchment on a baking tray (it should be big enough to fold over the fish and seal). Place the tomatoes, olives, capers, and garlic in the centre. Lay the fish on top.
Tuck the thyme and lemon slices inside the cavity and around the fish. Drizzle with olive oil, add the wine and a squeeze of lemon juice. Season generously.
Fold the parchment over the fish and crimp the edges tightly together to form a sealed parcel. Place on the baking tray.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes for a 700 g fish. The parcel will puff up dramatically. Bring to the table and cut open with scissors; serve directly from the parcel, spooning the juices over the fish.

items.fix: Crimp the edges very firmly. Any gap lets steam escape.

items.cause: Too long in the oven or fish was small
items.fix: Check at 18 minutes for a smaller fish. The flesh should flake easily when a skewer is inserted through the parcel.

items.cause: Too much wine or fish released a lot of water
items.fix: Pour the juices into a small pan and reduce briefly on the hob. Then spoon over the fish.

items.symptom: The olives or capers are too salty
items.fix: Rinse capers well under cold water. Use pitted olives in brine rather than heavily salted dry-cured olives.

content.text: Al cartoccio cooking appears throughout Italian cuisine, not just for fish: mushrooms, vegetables, and even pasta can be sealed in a parcel and baked. For fish, it is particularly associated with the Mediterranean coast and the islands. The sealed parcel is both a cooking technique (trapped steam, gentle heat) and a presentation device: the theatrical opening at the table releases the accumulated steam and the fragrance of wine, olives, and herbs. It is one of the most impressive things you can do with a simple whole fish.
